name: Hempen Rope
description:
A workmanlike coil of hemp rope with its ends whipped against fraying. It is useful for hauling, tying down loads and climbing when properly secured.

One purchase contains 50 feet. Under the 2014 rules the rope has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check. The rope alone does not establish a safe anchor, remove a climbing check or protect against falling.

weight.notes: Adjusted dry weight for one complete 50-foot coil; count additional coils separately.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1, Adventuring Gear: Rope. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.

name: Silk Rope
description:
A smooth, tightly braided silk rope that packs more lightly than hemp. Its soft finish makes it pleasant to handle, but it still requires sound knots and a secure anchor.

One purchase contains 50 feet. It has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check under the 2014 rope rules. The higher price buys lighter cordage, not an automatic bonus to climbing.

weight.notes: Adjusted dry weight for a complete 50-foot silk coil, half the project's hemp-rope weight.

name: Twine
description:
A small ball of twisted plant fibre for tying parcels, securing labels and marking a straight line. Its loose fibres take a simple knot readily.

The ball contains 100 feet. Twine is suitable for light lashings, not for supporting a climbing creature or arresting a fall. Cutting it into shorter lengths does not create more material.

weight.notes: Adjusted weight for 100 feet of fine twine; excludes a separate reel or container.

name: Grappling Hook
description:
A forged iron hook with three curved tines and an eye for a rope. It can catch an accessible ledge, beam or other suitable purchase.

Sold without rope. Throwing it into position and judging whether the hold will bear a climber remain matters for the GM; possession of a hook does not guarantee a secure anchor.

weight.notes: Adjusted weight for a compact three-tined iron hook; rope is separate.

name: Pitons
description:
Ten tapered iron pitons with eyes for cord or rope, wrapped together for sale. Each is intended to be driven into a suitable rock crack or timber to help establish an anchor.

The listed price and weight cover the entire bundle. Each piton accounts for 0.2 lb if the bundle is split. A hammer and rope are separate; the strength of an anchor depends on its placement and the supporting material.

weight.notes: Adjusted bundle weight: ten iron pitons at 0.2 lb each, including negligible wrapping.

name: Climber's Kit
description:
A compact climbing set containing specialised pitons, boot fittings, tough gloves and a harness. It is supplied as one kit; a separate rope is still useful and is not included in this purchase.

Using an action, you can secure yourself to an anchor. While secured, the 2014 kit rules limit a fall to 25 feet from that point and prevent climbing more than 25 feet away without releasing the anchor. The kit does not grant a climbing speed or an automatic successful climb.

weight.notes: Adjusted total for the harness, gloves, boot fittings and specialised pitons; excludes a separate rope.
